params.text:
The rocks along this stretch of coast were laid down as layers of sediment roughly 417–354 million years ago. Earth movements later squeezed and folded them: three generations of folds have been recorded in Bovisand Bay.

Source: Plymouth Sound, Shores and Cliffs (Wikipedia)

Look closely at the rock surface. The closely spaced planes are cleavage, formed as the rock was squeezed. In Bovisand Bay the cleavage dips at about 40 degrees towards the south.

Source: Plymouth Sound, Shores and Cliffs (Wikipedia)

Click the scene, then use W, A, S and D to move around the cove, Q and E to move down and up, and drag to look around. Hold Shift to move faster.

Press Home, or the reset button, to come back to this view.
